CYP2B, CYP4A and some CYP3 A enzyme inducers stimulate replicative DNA syntheis in rat liver, but not other CYP3A inducers.
CYP2B inducers stimulate DNA synthesis in rat liver and CYP3A inducers do not.

the CYP3A inducers, phenobarbitone, dexamethasome, troleandomycin, clotrimazole and miconazole, stimulate replicative DNA in rat liver, whereas CYP3A non-inducers, isoniazid and beta-naphtho-flavone, and the CYP3-inducer, barbituric-acid do not.

the effects of enzyme inducers on CYP isoforms and replicative DNA synthesis.
the effects of some enzyme inducers on hepatic DNA synthesis, CYP isoforms and the cytochrome P-450 content.
the effects of various inducers of CYP isoforms on replicative DNA in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CYP3A inducers are not mitogenic, although some CYP3As may be.
CYP2B, CYP3A, CYP1A, CYP2C, CYP2D, CYP2F and CYP4 enzymes are inducible, whereas CYP3A2, CFP and CYP1A1 enzymes are not inducible.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CYP2B enzyme inducers (i.e. NaPB, BNF, MCP and BA) stimulate both CYP2B isoform expression and replicative DNA synthesis.
only those enzyme inducers that increase the levels of both CYP3A1 and CYP3A2 in rat liver are likely to stimulate hepatocyte replication in vivo.
CYP2B, 4A, 3A and 1A isoforms may be involved in the regulation of liver growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
not all CYP3A inducers stimulate replicative DNA, and therefore the mechanism by which CYP3A induces hepatocarcinogenicity may not be via the mitogenic pathway.
